name: The Tamarinds of Wat Arun's Giants

location.address: Wat Arun Ratchawararam, Thanon Wang Doem, Bangkok Yai (gate of the ordination hall)

verified_sources: https://spacebar.th/lifestyle/six-legendary-heritage-tree (2024-06-22, says the pair still stands beside the giants)
https://thestandard.co/trees-over-100-years-old-in-bkk/ (2020-10-21, says the two were not planted together)

official_register.name: Rukkha Moradok khong Phaendin (Heritage Trees of the Land), Dept of Cultural Promotion, Ministry of Culture, 2017 list no. 10

access: Paid entry to Wat Arun: foreign visitors pay a small cash fee at the ticket counter by the gate (amount not verified), open daily 8:00 to 18:00 (watarunvisit.com); one ticket covers the ordination hall and the gate with the giants. Shoes off inside the hall. Dress code not verified.
transport: Cross-river ferry from Tha Tien pier (Chao Phraya Express N8), then walk through the grounds to the ordination hall gate; the exact crossing time was not verified.

location_site.name: Gate of the ordination hall (ubosot), Wat Arun, with the two giant guardians

verify_notes: Register entry 2017-10 (Thai name: Twin giant tamarinds of Wat Chaeng). Register gives no age, girth or height ('not specified'). Register history text: the tamarind beside the green giant Thotsakan (left in the photo) is already in Henri Mouhot's drawing in 'Travels in Siam, Cambodia and Laos 1858-1860' and an 1867 old photograph, so it predates 1858; the tamarind beside the white giant Sahatsadecha (right) was probably planted later, it appears on a postcard from the reign of Rama VII (1925-1934). The two were not planted together (also The Standard 2020). Both stand trimmed into a neat shape. Species is from the Thai common name (makham) only; tamarind is consistent with Thai-language descriptions. Alive: Spacebar 2024-06-22 says the pair still stands beside the giants; one iNaturalist tamarind observation labelled Wat Arun dated 2026-03-10 (observation 342189515, casual, cultivated, about 80 m east of the register point, not proven to be this tree). Register-only for dimensions; the Mouhot dating is the register's own claim, Mouhot book not seen. Register point 13.743675,100.488895 is the temple's centre (Commons photos of the prang geotag within 5 m), not the gate, so the pin is temple level: approximate. Pin not confirmed: no OSM tree node found (Overpass mirror 504, Nominatim empty). Age: the left tree is over about 165 years (1858 to 2026), basis is the register's reading of the Mouhot drawing. Thailand is not a covered country. Not a duplicate of any live Bangkok tree (bkk_001 to bkk_005 are 1 to 2 km away). Does not tip into hard rule 10: paid temple grounds are public.
